results.question: For each user, how many tasks are they assigned? Include users with none.
results.expected_sql:
SELECT u.full_name, COUNT(t.id) AS task_count
FROM users u
LEFT JOIN tasks t ON t.assigned_user_id = u.id
GROUP BY u.id, u.full_name
results.generated_sql: SELECT users.full_name, COUNT(tasks.id) AS task_count FROM users LEFT JOIN tasks ON tasks.assigned_user_id = users.id GROUP BY users.id, users.full_name ORDER BY users.full_name
results.raw_output: {"sql": "SELECT users.full_name, COUNT(tasks.id) AS task_count FROM users LEFT JOIN tasks ON tasks.assigned_user_id = users.id GROUP BY users.id, users.full_name ORDER BY users.full_name"}

results.question: For each blocked task, show the task name, the workflow name and the workflow owner's name.
results.expected_sql:
SELECT t.name AS task_name, w.name AS workflow_name, o.full_name AS owner
FROM tasks t
JOIN workflows w ON w.id = t.workflow_id
JOIN users o ON o.id = w.owner_user_id
WHERE t.status = 'BLOCKED'
results.generated_sql: SELECT t.name AS task_name, w.name AS workflow_name, u.full_name AS workflow_owner_name FROM tasks t JOIN workflows w ON w.id = t.workflow_id JOIN users u ON u.id = w.owner_user_id WHERE t.status = 'BLOCKED'

results.question: Work out how many unfinished tasks each user has, then list the users with more than 2 of them.
results.expected_sql:
WITH open_counts AS (
  SELECT assigned_user_id, COUNT(*) AS open_tasks
  FROM tasks
  WHERE status <> 'COMPLETED' AND assigned_user_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY assigned_user_id
)
SELECT u.full_name, oc.open_tasks
FROM open_counts oc
JOIN users u ON u.id = oc.assigned_user_id
WHERE oc.open_tasks > 2
results.generated_sql:
SELECT u.id, u.full_name, COUNT(t.id) AS unfinished_task_count
FROM users u
JOIN tasks t ON t.assigned_user_id = u.id
WHERE t.status <> 'COMPLETED'
GROUP BY u.id, u.full_name
HAVING COUNT(t.id) > 2
ORDER BY unfinished_task_count DESC
results.raw_output:
{"sql": "SELECT u.id, u.full_name, COUNT(t.id) AS unfinished_task_count
FROM users u
JOIN tasks t ON t.assigned_user_id = u.id
WHERE t.status <> 'COMPLETED'
GROUP BY u.id, u.full_name
HAVING COUNT(t.id) > 2
ORDER BY unfinished_task_count DESC"}

results.question: Which workflows are healthy, meaning they have no overdue and no blocked tasks?
results.expected_sql:
SELECT w.name
FROM workflows w
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM tasks t
  WHERE t.workflow_id = w.id
    AND (t.status = 'BLOCKED'
         OR (t.due_date < CURRENT_DATE AND t.status <> 'COMPLETED'))
)
results.generated_sql: SELECT w.id, w.name FROM workflows w WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM tasks t WHERE t.workflow_id = w.id AND t.due_date < CURRENT_DATE AND t.status <> 'COMPLETED') AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM tasks t WHERE t.workflow_id = w.id AND t.status = 'BLOCKED') ORDER BY w.name
results.raw_output: {"sql": "SELECT w.id, w.name FROM workflows w WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM tasks t WHERE t.workflow_id = w.id AND t.due_date < CURRENT_DATE AND t.status <> 'COMPLETED') AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM tasks t WHERE t.workflow_id = w.id AND t.status = 'BLOCKED') ORDER BY w.name"}

results.question: How much work is still outstanding in each workflow?

FROM workflows w
LEFT JOIN tasks t
       ON t.workflow_id = w.id AND t.status <> 'COMPLETED'
GROUP BY w.id, w.name
results.generated_sql: SELECT workflows.id AS workflow_id, workflows.name AS workflow_name, COUNT(tasks.id) FILTER (WHERE tasks.status <> 'COMPLETED') AS outstanding_tasks FROM workflows LEFT JOIN tasks ON tasks.workflow_id = workflows.id GROUP BY workflows.id, workflows.name ORDER BY outstanding_tasks DESC
